mentl/321533b:
infer_program_converged ran `src |> frontend` twice, and frontend is
`source |> lex |> parse_program`, so every compile lexed the whole
concatenated program twice — 57,881 lines of it on the wheel's own
self-compile.

The two parses are load-bearing and stay. The final walks a fresh
generation of nodes, which is exactly what pstart = graph_next() reads
as its lower bound, so parsing once and judging one tree twice would
collapse the boundary the tower is built on. The two lexes never were: a
token is a value and mints nothing. This is not an improvement to the
condemned tower — its judgment, cadence and two generations are
untouched, and when rung 3 deletes the second pass this seam loses a
caller rather than needing unpicking.

Two kills came with it, both larger than the landing.

Lex is not the floor. Deleting a whole-program lex moved the fixture
0.00s, seven settled reads at 0.78s median. The deletion is kept because
it is one, not because it paid. It also kills the token-carry design the
previous pin named: carrying tokens to avoid a lex buys nothing and
would have paid the span re-basing dep for it.

The floor is traversing the tokens. A probe replacing import_edges' body
with a literal measured 0.50s against 0.78s — the whole 0.28s. Rewriting
that traversal as a position recursion, allocating on the four import
hits instead of a product per token, measured identical, so it is not
the fold or the tuple or the indirect call. It is the walk, roughly 11µs
a token over ~25k tokens, which indicts per-element traversal in the
substrate and would tax the parser the same way. The position form was
reverted: its only justification was a speedup that did not exist.

mentl/325470d:
All five shape-bearing pattern arms (literal, constructor, tuple, list,
record) bound the pattern's shape directly onto the scrutinee's own
node, and graph_bind overwrites: every destructure DISCARDED the
scrutinee's proven type and re-minted fresh free vars. The binders
never touched the proven element/payload types, so they floored to
word representation unless a later use happened to ground them — the
tuple writer stored f64 at width-summed offsets while the pattern
reader loaded words at word offsets, the split-truth miscompile
mn-fanout-destructure-float pins (bare a + b, no grounding use). The
arms' own comments claimed the unification semantics the code lacked.

constrain_scrutinee is the one home: bind the pattern's shape onto a
fresh node, unify it with the scrutinee. Proven types flow into
binders; an arity or shape mismatch is a diagnostic, never a silent
retype. On the wheel's own self-compile this resolves ~4,400

(the 581a92f class — an unregistered nominal erasing the element

f64 payload is 8 inline bytes at an aligned offset. The word-slot size
under-allocated every f64-payload variant by 4+ bytes, so the next
allocation clobbered the payload's high half: every float literal m3

parse_float's input is byte-perfect; int_part=2, dot_pos=1, frac=0.5,
base=2.5 all correct INSIDE parse_float_body — the value died in the
token record. Size is now product_byte_size_acc(fields, 0, n, 4) — the
same fold the stores, variant_payload_offset, and the eq/match-bind
offsets read (one fold, four readers). All-i32 variants are
